long_biography.plain_text:
Berrebi grew up around maritime agencies established by his grandfather and expanded by his father in Tunisia. He left for France, studied at ESCP and joined SGS, where a timber-transport assignment introduced him to chartering between the Congo and Europe. A client encouraged him to strike out alone, and he formed Unishipping in 1986.

Without owning ships at first, Berrebi moved cargo to North Africa and the Caribbean on chartered tonnage. He later acquired a roll-on/roll-off vessel and shifted his focus toward Mexico and the United States, carrying industrial goods and developing regular services. Baja Ferries extended that model to freight and passenger routes across the Gulf of California. His work also included Caribbean services and investment in specialist boatbuilding, but commercial ferries remained the centre of his operating identity.

proposed_details.existing_value:
Originally from Tunisia, Mr. Berrebi hails from a family with deep roots in shipping. His grandfather established VN BERREBI in Sfax, Tunisia, in 1921, and his father later expanded the business in the 1960s.

Mr. Berrebi went on to found Unishipping and currently serves as the Chairman of Baja Ferries, a ferry operator headquartered in La Paz, Mexico. Baja Ferries provides both cargo and passenger services across the Gulf of California, linking the Baja California Peninsula with mainland Mexico.

In February 2022, Daniel Berrebi and his wife, Carmen Alcaraz Gomes Berrebi, sold their waterfront estate in Coral Gables, Florida, for $13.3 million.

Now a U.S. citizen, Mr. Berrebi splits his time between Miami and Baja California, Mexico.
